title: rest/analytics: dataset query and dataset tools resolve the dataset by package (ADR-0150 D3; reader before #31700)
body:
epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic:** ADR-0150 (#31527). This card adds a reader that #31700 needs before it narrows. Found by #31700 step 0 (amendment 6760386575, project file `server-seat3/31700-step0.md`, measured on `main` at 48f18b58 with showcase plus `com.qa.bare.alpha` (namespace `alpha`) and `com.qa.bare.beta` (namespace `beta`), each holding one name). Today the cold boot only warns, so this shape boots on main.
**Blocks:** #31700. **Lane:** `domain:server`.

## dataset: analytics query and dataset tools resolve the dataset by ADR-0150 D3

**Today:** `POST /analytics/dataset/query` with `datasetName` (rest `analytics-routes.ts:235`) and the dataset AI tools use `getMetaItems` plus `list.find(name)`, so they run alpha's dataset (`FROM "alpha_item"`). The bare `GET /meta/dataset/NAME` serves the first holder.
**Do:**
- **Query and tools:** read through the package-scoped resolver, never `list.find`. The HTTP query reads with no caller unless the request names a package (`?package=`, or a namespaced name). A tool call's caller is the agent's own package.
- **Bare read:** add `dataset` to `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`.

**Rule (D3):** a package caller resolves to its own item, then to the one holder in its closure plus `sys`, and otherwise refuses. A read with no caller takes the environment item, then the one package holder, and otherwise answers 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming every candidate. It never takes the first or last match. The qualified addresses (`/meta/:type/:ns/:name`, `?package=`, `_env`) reach each holder.
**Clause-②:** the seat declares it. A two-holder read changes from "first holder" to 409, which narrows behaviour for a shape that only boots with a warning. The first-party census is 0, so give it.
**Pins:** two packages and two namespaces with one name: each caller gets its own item, and a read with no caller answers 409 naming both. Ablating the resolver turns the pins red.
**Epic red-line review before landing.**
